title: Congruence and Similarity
seo_title: Grade 8 Congruence and Similarity Worksheets: Rigid Motions, Dilations, Scale Factor, AA
standard_text: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 congruence and similarity worksheets: congruent figures and rigid motions, similar figures and dilations, sequences of moves, scale factors and missing sides, angle-angle similarity and shadow problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Congruent: same size and shape (rigid motions). Similar: same shape (rigid motions and a dilation).
key_sub: In similar figures, angles are equal and sides are multiplied by the same scale factor.
body_html:
Congruent and similar

WordMeaningMoves
Congruent (≅)same size and same shapetranslations, reflections, rotations
Similar (~)same shape, maybe a different sizerigid motions plus a dilation

In similar figures, matching angles are equal and matching sides are in proportion. The scale factor is new side ÷ old side.

Example

Triangles 3-4-5 and 6-8-10 are similar. A side of 7 in the first matches what in a similar triangle with scale factor 2?

Multiply by the scale factor: 7 × 2.

Answer: 14

Angle-angle (AA)

If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar. Shadow problems use this: a person and a tree with their shadows make similar triangles.

Common mistakes

  • Adding instead of multiplying: a 2 × 3 rectangle doubled is 4 × 6, not 4 × 5.
  • Matching the wrong sides: match shortest with shortest.
  • Thinking similar means congruent. Similar figures can be different sizes.
  • Forgetting that area scales by k², not k.

faq.q: What is the difference between congruent and similar?
faq.a: Congruent figures have the same size and shape. Similar figures have the same shape, but can be different sizes.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side in similar figures?
faq.a: Find the scale factor by dividing two matching sides, then multiply the side you know by it.
If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another, the triangles are similar.

faq.q: What happens to area when a figure is dilated?
faq.a: Lengths and perimeter are multiplied by the scale factor k, but area is multiplied by k².

items.q: Which moves always give a congruent figure?
items.e: These rigid motions keep size and shape: translations, reflections and rotations.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is a reflection over the y-axis, so the size and shape stay the same. Congruent.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: Every side is twice as long (a dilation by 2): same shape, different size. Similar but not congruent.

items.q: Two figures are similar. Which must be true?
c: They are in the same place
items.e: Similar figures have the same shape: their angles are equal and their sides are in proportion.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is a translation: only the position changes. Congruent.

items.q: Two triangles have sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 10. How are they related?
items.e: Each side doubled: scale factor 2. Similar but not congruent.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is a rotation of 180°: same size and shape. Congruent.

items.q: Two triangles have sides 3, 4, 5 and 5, 4, 3. How are they related?
items.e: The same three side lengths: Congruent.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: One leg changed from 2 to 4 but the other stayed 3: the shape changed. Neither.

items.q: Two triangles have sides 3, 4, 5 and 4, 5, 6. How are they related?
items.e: 4/3, 5/4 and 6/5 are not equal: Neither.

items.q: Are all congruent figures similar?
items.e: Same size and shape means also same shape: yes, with scale factor 1.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: The legs are 4 and 3 instead of 3 and 2: not the same shape. Neither.

items.q: Are all similar figures congruent?
c: No, they can be different sizes
items.e: A small square and a big square are similar but not congruent: no, they can be different sizes.

items.q: A photo 4 in. × 6 in. is enlarged to 8 in. × 12 in. Is the enlargement similar?
items.e: 8/4 = 12/6 = 2: yes, scale factor 2.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is a 90° rotation: same size and shape. Congruent.

items.q: Are any two squares similar?
c: Only if they are the same size
items.e: All squares have 4 right angles and sides in the same ratio: yes, always.

items.q: How are the red and blue triangles related?
items.e: It is dilated by 2 and turned 180°: same shape, bigger size. Similar but not congruent.

items.q: Are any two rectangles similar?
c: Only if they have equal perimeters
items.e: A 1 × 2 rectangle and a 1 × 5 rectangle have different shapes: not always.

items.q: A figure is dilated by 3 and then rotated. Compared with the first figure, the result is …
items.e: The dilation changes the size, the rotation keeps the shape: similar.

items.q: A figure is reflected and then translated. Compared with the first figure, the result is …
items.e: Both moves are rigid: congruent.

items.q: Point (1, 2) is mapped to (4, 2). Which single move could do this?
items.e: Every point moves 3 to the right: a translation 3 units right.

items.q: Point (2, 3) is mapped to (−2, 3). Which single move could do this?
items.e: x changes sign, y stays: a reflection over the y-axis.

items.q: Point (2, 3) is mapped to (−2, −3). Which single move could do this?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Both signs change: a rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: To show two figures are congruent, you need …
c: a sequence of rigid motions that maps one onto the other
a dilation that maps one onto the other
items.e: Congruent means a sequence of rigid motions that maps one onto the other.

items.q: Point (2, 3) is mapped to (6, 9). Which single move could do this?
c: A translation 4 right and 6 up only
A dilation by 3 from the origin
items.e: Both coordinates are multiplied by 3: a dilation by 3 from the origin.

items.q: Triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF. Which side matches AB?
items.e: Corresponding letters match: A↔D, B↔E, so AB ↔ DE.

items.q: Point (2, 3) is mapped to (3, −2). Which single move could do this?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: (x, y) → (y, −x) is a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin.

items.q: Point (2, 3) is mapped to (−3, 2). Which single move could do this?
c: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
items.e: (x, y) → (−y, x) is a rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

items.q: Triangle ABC ~ triangle XYZ. Which angle equals angle B?
items.e: B is the second letter, Y is the second letter: angle Y.

items.q: Start at (1, 2). First reflect over the x-axis, then translate 3 right. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (4, −2).

items.q: To show two figures are similar, you can use …
items.e: Similar means you can map one onto the other with rigid motions and one dilation.

items.q: Start at (3, 1). First rotate 180° about the origin, then translate 2 up. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (−3, 1).

items.q: Start at (2, 4). First dilate by 1/2 from the origin, then reflect over the y-axis. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (−1, 2).

items.q: A figure is rotated 90° and then rotated 90° again (same direction, same center). One move that does the same is …
items.e: 90° + 90° = a rotation of 180°.

items.q: Start at (−1, 3). First translate 4 right, then reflect over the x-axis. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (3, −3).

items.q: Does the order of a translation and a reflection matter?
c: It always gives the same point
Sometimes, it can give a different result
items.e: Reflect then translate can land somewhere else than translate then reflect: sometimes, it can give a different result.

items.q: Start at (4, −2). First reflect over the y-axis, then rotate 180° about the origin. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (4, 2).

items.q: Start at (1, 1). First dilate by 3 from the origin, then translate 1 left and 2 down. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (2, 1).

items.q: Start at (5, 0). First rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translate 2 left. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (−2, 5).

items.q: Start at (−2, −3). First reflect over the x-axis, then reflect over the y-axis. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do the moves in order. The point ends at (2, 3).

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 3, 4 and 5. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 3. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Multiply: 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: Rectangle A is 4 cm wide and 6 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 10 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 52. Height = 6 × 52 = 15 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 6, 8 and 10. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 3 that matches the side of 6. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 8?
items.e: Scale factor = 3 ÷ 6 = 12. Multiply: 8 × 12 = 4.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 cm wide and 5 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 12 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Height = 5 × 4 = 20 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 12 and 13. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 36 that matches the side of 12. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Multiply: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Two similar triangles have scale factor 3. The small one has perimeter 12 cm. What is the perimeter of the large one?
items.e: Perimeter scales by the same factor: 12 × 3 = 36 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 4, 6 and 7. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 4. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 7?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 4 = 32. Multiply: 7 × 32 = 10.5.

items.q: Rectangle A is 8 cm wide and 12 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 6 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 8 = 34. Height = 12 × 34 = 9 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 9, 12 and 15. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 4 that matches the side of 12. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 9?
items.e: Scale factor = 4 ÷ 12 = 13. Multiply: 9 × 13 = 3.

items.q: Two similar figures have scale factor 2. The small one has area 10 cm². What is the area of the large one?
items.e: Area scales by the square of the factor: 10 × 2² = 40 cm².

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 2, 5 and 6. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 8 that matches the side of 2. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Multiply: 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: Rectangle A is 5 cm wide and 8 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 15 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Height = 8 × 3 = 24 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 8, 10 and 14. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 12 that matches the side of 8. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 10?
items.e: Scale factor = 12 ÷ 8 = 32. Multiply: 10 × 32 = 15.

items.q: A map uses a scale factor of 1/1,000. A road is 8 cm on the map. How long is it in real life?
Triangle 1 has sides 7, 7 and 10. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 14 that matches the side of 7. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 10?
items.e: Scale factor = 14 ÷ 7 = 2. Multiply: 10 × 2 = 20.

items.q: Rectangle A is 6 cm wide and 9 cm tall. Rectangle B is similar and 4 cm wide. How tall is Rectangle B?
items.e: Scale factor = 4 ÷ 6 = 23. Height = 9 × 23 = 6 cm.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 10, 15 and 20. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 15. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 10?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 15 = 25. Multiply: 10 × 25 = 4.

items.q: A model car is 1/24 of the real size. The model is 18 cm long. How long is the real car?
Triangle 1 has sides 6, 9 and 12. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 8 that matches the side of 6. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 12?
items.e: Scale factor = 8 ÷ 6 = 43. Multiply: 12 × 43 = 16.

items.q: Leo says a 2 × 3 rectangle and a 4 × 5 rectangle are similar because he added 2 to each side. Is he right?
c: No, you must multiply, not add
items.e: 4/2 = 2 but 5/3 ≠ 2: no, you must multiply, not add.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 50° and 60°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 40° and 70°. Triangle 2 has angles 70° and 40°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 70° and 70°. Triangle 1: 40°, 70°, 70°. Triangle 2: 70°, 40°, 70°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 35° and 90°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 35° − 90° = 55°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 50° and 60°. Triangle 2 has angles 50° and 75°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 70° and 55°. Triangle 1: 50°, 60°, 70°. Triangle 2: 50°, 75°, 55°. No, the angles are different.

items.q: Why are two triangles with two equal angles always similar?
c: The third angles must also be equal
items.e: Angles add to 180°, so the third angles match too: the third angles must also be equal.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 72° and 48°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 72° − 48° = 60°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 90° and 30°. Triangle 2 has angles 60° and 90°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 60° and 30°. Triangle 1: 90°, 30°, 60°. Triangle 2: 60°, 90°, 30°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 40° and 40°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 40° − 40° = 100°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 45° and 45°. Triangle 2 has angles 45° and 90°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 90° and 45°. Triangle 1: 45°, 45°, 90°. Triangle 2: 45°, 90°, 45°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts off a small triangle. Is the small triangle similar to the big one?
items.e: Parallel lines make equal corresponding angles: yes, they share angles.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 100° and 30°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 100° − 30° = 50°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 35° and 80°. Triangle 2 has angles 35° and 75°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 65° and 70°. Triangle 1: 35°, 80°, 65°. Triangle 2: 35°, 75°, 70°. No, the angles are different.

items.q: A 6-ft man casts a 4-ft shadow. At the same time a tree casts a 20-ft shadow. How tall is the tree?
items.e: The triangles are similar: 6/4 = h/20, so h = 20 × 1.5 = 30 ft.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 65° and 55°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 65° − 55° = 60°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 100° and 50°. Triangle 2 has angles 30° and 100°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 30° and 50°. Triangle 1: 100°, 50°, 30°. Triangle 2: 30°, 100°, 50°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: A 1-m stick casts a 1.5-m shadow. A pole casts a 9-m shadow. How tall is the pole?
Two triangles are similar. One has angles 25° and 120°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 25° − 120° = 35°.

items.q: A 5-ft girl casts a 3-ft shadow. A flagpole casts a 12-ft shadow. How tall is the flagpole?
Two triangles are similar. One has angles 90° and 45°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 90° − 45° = 45°.

items.q: Two right triangles each have a 30° angle. Are they similar?
c: Only if the hypotenuses are equal
items.e: Both have 90° and 30° (so also 60°): AA. Yes.

items.q: A rectangle is 5 by 8. A similar rectangle has a short side of 15. What is its long side?
items.e: Scale factor 3: 8 × 3 = 24.

items.q: Triangle A has sides 3, 4, 5. Triangle B has sides 9, 12, 15. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 3, 3, 3. Similar, scale factor 3.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 18 and area 15. It is dilated by 2. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 2 = 36. Area × (2)² = 60. Perimeter 36, area 60.

items.q: A triangle’s sides are 6, 9 and 12. A similar triangle’s shortest side is 4. What is its longest side?
Triangle A has sides 2, 2, 3. Triangle B has sides 2, 3, 2. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 1, 1, 1. Congruent.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 10 and area 4. It is dilated by 3. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 3 = 30. Area × (3)² = 36. Perimeter 30, area 36.

items.q: A door is 2 m tall and 0.8 m wide. A model door is 10 cm tall. How wide is it?
items.e: Scale: 10 cm for 200 cm, so 1/20. 80 cm ÷ 20 = 4 cm.

items.q: Triangle A has sides 5, 6, 7. Triangle B has sides 10, 12, 15. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 2, 2, 2 17. Neither.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 40 and area 64. It is dilated by 12. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 12 = 20. Area × (12)² = 16. Perimeter 20, area 16.

items.q: Two similar cylinders: one is twice as tall. How many times as much area does a matching face have?
items.e: Area scales by 2² = 4 times.

items.q: Triangle A has sides 4, 4, 4. Triangle B has sides 7, 7, 7. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 1 34, 1 34, 1 34. Similar, scale factor 7/4.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 7 and area 2. It is dilated by 4. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 4 = 28. Area × (4)² = 32. Perimeter 28, area 32.

items.q: Triangle PQR ≅ triangle STU. PQ = 7 cm and angle Q = 50°. Which is true?
items.e: P↔S, Q↔T, R↔U, so ST = 7 cm and angle T = 50°.

items.q: Triangle A has sides 6, 8, 9. Triangle B has sides 3, 4, 4.5. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 12, 12, 12. Similar, scale factor 1/2.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 12 and area 6. It is dilated by 5. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 5 = 60. Area × (5)² = 150. Perimeter 60, area 150.

items.q: A 3-4-5 triangle is dilated by 2.5. What are the new sides?
items.e: Multiply each side by 2.5: 7.5, 10, 12.5.

items.q: Triangle A has sides 5, 5, 8. Triangle B has sides 10, 10, 12. How are they related?
items.e: Compare matching sides (smallest with smallest): ratios 2, 2, 1 12. Neither.

items.q: A figure has perimeter 27 and area 36. It is dilated by 13. What are the new perimeter and area?
items.e: Perimeter × 13 = 9. Area × (13)² = 4. Perimeter 9, area 4.

items.q: Ana says two triangles with all sides equal to 5 and all sides equal to 6 are not similar. Is she right?
c: No, all equilateral triangles are similar
items.e: Every equilateral triangle has 60° angles: no, all equilateral triangles are similar.

items.q: A shape is dilated by 1. What is the result?
items.e: Scale factor 1 keeps the size: a congruent shape.
